perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- Christian is a police officer and has been close friends with Jonathan since childhood. He trusts Jonathan and often values his advice.
- Christian noticed Jonathan acting differently and came to believe Jonathan was hiding something important. This made him anxious and suspicious. He arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- At the meeting, Christian heard Jonathan say he could trust him, then admit that he had been hiding something: Jonathan is in trouble and did not know how to tell Christian.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered to help and told Jonathan they could face it together. Jonathan replied that the situation is complicated, he does not want to drag Christian into it, but he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian suspected Jonathan’s trouble might involve criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. Jonathan said he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself. Christian decided to look into it discreetly.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan was being framed. He told Jonathan this, said he had leads, and planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian later came to believe the real culprit was someone both he and Jonathan knew and trusted. He told Jonathan this and decided to confront the culprit and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him that the person is dangerous but said he trusts Christian.
- The specific identity/name of the real culprit is not stated in the provided dialogue, though Christian claims to have found out who it is.
